Picture: High above a dark, heaving sea under racing storm clouds, the North Wind strides through the sky with his cloud cloak streaming and bends down to talk to the Young King, who flies beside him in a tall grey felt hat, a long dark-grey hooded cloak and tall brown boots, a tiny gold ring glinting in his hair. Far ahead on the horizon gleams a shore as white as snow.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Young King: A stocky, wide-shouldered young king of about twenty-one with a frank, square face, a bumpy nose, grey-green eyes that crinkle when he laughs, short, wavy brown hair and short brown stubble along his jaw. He wears a small, plain gold crown with five points and a long white wool cloak bordered with silver embroidery of little waves over a chunky cream cabled sweater, dark-blue breeches and knee-high boots of tan leather.
- the North Wind: A tall, lean, long-limbed storm giant, three times as tall as a man, with a long, bony, windburnt face, hollow cheeks, a long thin nose, a wide mouth pursed to blow and bright, shining silver eyes. His wild, tangled slate-grey hair and long, wispy beard stream sideways as if in a gale. He wears a huge, billowing cloak made of dark-grey storm clouds, torn into ragged wisps at the edges, and from the knees down he fades into swirling grey mist.

Story world: Old Norway by the sea. The fisherman's small grey log cottage with a turf roof stands on the rocky shore right below the royal castle, a long hall of dark timber and grey stone. His boat is a small, tarred, dark-brown rowing boat with two oars. Far across the sea lies Whiteland, whose shore is sand as white as snow, with a dark spruce forest behind it and, in the forest, a grim grey castle with two lions in its gateway. The wishing ring is a plain gold ring, and the ring the queen ties into his hair is a tiny gold ring. The magic hat, cloak and boots are a tall grey felt hat, a long dark-grey hooded cloak and tall brown boots, and the magic skis are long and wooden, with curled tips.

This story's season, light and colours: The cold, clear light of the far north in winter: a copper-red sunset over a dark sea at the start, then the snow-white shore of Whiteland under a pale pearl-grey sky, spruce forest heavy with snow and long blue twilights. characters.name: The Fisherman’s Son (Young King)
characters.description: A fisherman’s child raised by the king, brave enough to endure trolls’ torment to free the princesses, yet fated to lose and reclaim his queen through hard-won wisdom.
characters.look: A stocky, wide-shouldered young man of about twenty with a frank, square face, a bumpy nose, grey-green eyes that crinkle when he laughs, short, wavy brown hair and short brown stubble along his jaw. He wears a chunky, cream-coloured hand-knitted wool sweater with a cabled pattern, dark-blue homespun breeches and knee-high boots of tan leather, and a red handkerchief with white spots pokes out of his pocket.

characters.name: The Young King
characters.description: The fisherman’s son once the youngest princess has made him her king. He breaks his promise and must search the whole world for the way back to Whiteland.
characters.look: A stocky, wide-shouldered young king of about twenty-one with a frank, square face, a bumpy nose, grey-green eyes that crinkle when he laughs, short, wavy brown hair and short brown stubble along his jaw. He wears a small, plain gold crown with five points and a long white wool cloak bordered with silver embroidery of little waves over a chunky cream cabled sweater, dark-blue breeches and knee-high boots of tan leather.

characters.name: The Fisherman
characters.description: The boy’s father, who fishes for the king’s table and promises away what he doesn’t know his wife is carrying.
characters.look: A lean, wiry fisherman of about forty-five with a long, weather-beaten face, deep laughter lines, a sharp nose, kind, crinkly blue eyes and a long, drooping black moustache but no beard. He wears a round, brimless sealskin cap, a thick grey wool jumper under a long, stiff apron of dark oiled leather, grey breeches tucked into heavy wooden-soled boots, and a coil of fishing line at his belt.

characters.name: The Youngest Princess of Whiteland (The Queen)
characters.description: The cleverest of the three sisters, she guides the hero through the trolls’ trial, becomes his queen, and sets the crucial condition he tragically breaks.
characters.look: A calm, thoughtful princess of about nineteen with a softly rounded chin, a small nose with a slight upturn, sea-grey eyes under soft brows, a quiet, knowing half-smile and long, wavy golden hair that flows down to her waist. A thin silver circlet with one pearl rests on her brow. She wears a plain sky-blue wool dress with long, close-fitting sleeves, a narrow belt of silver links and a hem sewn with small silver stars.

characters.name: The Queen of Whiteland
characters.description: The youngest princess as queen. She gives the young king a wishing ring, but must go home when he breaks his promise.
characters.look: A calm young queen of about nineteen with a softly rounded chin, a small nose with a slight upturn, sea-grey eyes under soft brows, a quiet, knowing half-smile and long, wavy golden hair that flows down to her waist. She wears a tall gold crown set with pale-blue stones, a sky-blue gown with a bodice laced with silver cord and a long train, and a short white fur cape fastened with a round silver clasp.

characters.name: The Nine-Headed Troll
characters.description: The worst of the three trolls who buried the princesses. It whips the boy until he faints, but its own fury breaks the jar of ointment that saves him.
characters.look: An enormous troll that fills a room up to the ceiling, with a huge, round, lumpy body of pale, chalky-cream hide blotched with big peat-brown patches like an old birch stump, stumpy legs and big round hands. Nine heads grow in a ring around the top of its body like a crown of boulders, each with a broad pinkish snout, small sleepy brown eyes, floppy ears and a wide mouth. It wears a huge, ragged smock of faded red-and-white checked homespun.

characters.name: The North Wind
characters.description: A roaring, personified force of nature who helps the young king drive away the false suitor and reclaim the castle.
characters.look: A tall, lean, long-limbed storm giant, three times as tall as a man, with a long, bony, windburnt face, hollow cheeks, a long thin nose, a wide mouth pursed to blow and bright, shining silver eyes. His wild, tangled slate-grey hair and long, wispy beard stream sideways as if in a gale. He wears a huge, billowing cloak made of dark-grey storm clouds, torn into ragged wisps at the edges, and from the knees down he fades into swirling grey mist.

places.name: the Forest Castle
places.look: A grim old castle of grey stone standing in dark spruce forest just behind a shore of snow-white sand: steep dark roofs, three narrow towers, small deep-set windows and a high outer wall with a wide arched gateway. Inside the wall, a broad flight of stone steps leads up to a heavy arched oak door. Snow lies on the roofs and on the spruces all around.

Picture: Out on a wide brown bog with patches of snow, three ragged, ancient brothers with long, tangled white beards, who have been fighting for a hundred years, stop in the middle of a scuffle and gape. In front of them, the Young King, now wearing a tall grey felt hat, a long dark-grey hooded cloak and tall brown boots, is rising into the air and fading away like smoke, until the bog shows through him.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Young King: A stocky, wide-shouldered young king of about twenty-one with a frank, square face, a bumpy nose, grey-green eyes that crinkle when he laughs, short, wavy brown hair and short brown stubble along his jaw. He wears a small, plain gold crown with five points and a long white wool cloak bordered with silver embroidery of little waves over a chunky cream cabled sweater, dark-blue breeches and knee-high boots of tan leather.

Story world: Old Norway by the sea. The fisherman's small grey log cottage with a turf roof stands on the rocky shore right below the royal castle, a long hall of dark timber and grey stone. His boat is a small, tarred, dark-brown rowing boat with two oars. Far across the sea lies Whiteland, whose shore is sand as white as snow, with a dark spruce forest behind it and, in the forest, a grim grey castle with two lions in its gateway. The wishing ring is a plain gold ring, and the ring the queen ties into his hair is a tiny gold ring. The magic hat, cloak and boots are a tall grey felt hat, a long dark-grey hooded cloak and tall brown boots, and the magic skis are long and wooden, with curled tips.

This story's season, light and colours: The cold, clear light of the far north in winter: a copper-red sunset over a dark sea at the start, then the snow-white shore of Whiteland under a pale pearl-grey sky, spruce forest heavy with snow and long blue twilights. On the long journey: deep snow on blue mountains, a steel-grey sea and wild, racing storm clouds with flying snow. Accents: the queen’s sky blue and the gold of rings and crowns.

Art style: Classic Norwegian folk-tale book illustration: fine pen-and-ink line work with transparent watercolour washes on warm, slightly textured off-white paper, in the tradition of 19th-century Scandinavian book illustration, like the plates of an old printed book of folk tales, with a deep red that comes back as the accent. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Naturalistic proportions and expressive, characterful faces; every character has their own face, build, age and hair exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Muted natural palette of fjord teal, slate blue, moss green, lichen grey, honey ochre, lingonberry red, ink black and birch white, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours, with the warm cream paper showing through the washes, with dramatic Nordic light: low sun, long shadows, blue dusk and firelight. Old rural Norway: dark spruce and pine forests, steep mountains, fjords, turf-roofed log farms, carved wood, homespun wool and linen. Trolls are enormous, ancient and earthy, like pieces of the landscape come alive, made of moss, bark, stone and lichen, and more grotesque-comic than frightening. Kings and princesses wear modest medieval finery. Careful composition with depth and atmosphere, one clear focal point and room for the landscape. Not cute or cartoonish, not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

illustrations.caption: When he showed her the ring, she was glad with all her heart.
